results.content:
The first post-election Economist/YouGov survey, conducted November 4–6 among 3,166 registered voters, found Trump with 36 percent approval and 62 percent disapproval, a net rating of –26.

Fifty percent strongly disapproved while 17 percent strongly approved. The result marked a seven-point deterioration from the pollster's final pre-election survey.

An important part of the background for elections is the unpopularity of President Donald Trump. 39% of registered voters strongly or somewhat approve of Trump's job performance, and 58% disapprove — a net job approval of -19. That's lower than Trump's -7 net approval at this point in 2018 and Joe Biden's of -8 in late October 2022.
